transcript:
User: Oh you remind me of my nephew — he's in prison again, third time, anyway my chihuahua needs surgery which costs more than my car, what was I saying? Oh! My neighbor's tree fell on my fence in 2019...
Agent: Oh wow—yeah, that’s a lot all at once, I hear you. What made you call Dialux today?
User: Oh, I was just reminded of that time the basement flooded during a storm, such a mess!
Agent: Got it—storms can get chaotic fast. Did you come across Dialux because you’re trying to make sure storm-related calls (like leaks or emergency tarping) don’t get missed, or was it something else?
User: Storms are wild! Oh, speaking of wild, my cat once chased a squirrel right into the house!
Agent: Mhm—cats are something else. Real quick, what kind of business are you in?
User: You know, my sister's bakery just won an award! Anyway, my allergies are acting up today.
Agent: Nice—that’s awesome for your sister. Are you calling for your sister’s bakery, or for a different business?
User: My sister's bakery is thriving! But I'm actually calling about something else. My knee's been acting up, too.
Agent: Got it—you’re calling about something else. Where did you hear about Dialux—did you see an ad, find us on Google, or did someone refer you?
User: Oh, I can't recall exactly. Maybe it was during my morning coffee? Speaking of which, I need a refill!
Agent: Got it. What did you hope Dialux would help with—missing calls, booking more jobs, or something else?
User: Oh, I was thinking about missing calls, but then our dog got into my garden again. Such a rascal!
Agent: Got it—missing calls. What’s been happening that’s making you look at this right now?
User: Well, I was trying to catch up on things, but then my brother's car broke down—always something!
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—always something. When that happens and you’re tied up, what happens to your calls—do they go to voicemail or does someone grab them?
User: Oh, my voicemails pile up, like when my son had chickenpox and I missed everything! How's the weather there?
Agent: Makes sense—those voicemails piling up is exactly what I mean. Roughly how many calls a day would you say end up going to voicemail?
User: Oh, probably around ten. Speaking of calls, my mom just called about her new hobby, bird watching!
Agent: Got it—around ten a day hitting voicemail. When those callers don’t get a quick answer, do you notice they ever just book with someone else?
User: You know, that reminds me of my cousin's wedding mix-up! It's hard to say, really.
Agent: Got it—it’s hard to track sometimes. When those calls hit voicemail, do most people leave a message, or do they usually hang up and disappear?
User: Oh, most hang up! It’s like my garden gnome collection—always disappearing without a trace!
Agent: Got it—so most hang up and disappear, which usually means they’re calling the next place. What kind of business is this for?
User: Oh, my cousin's cat cafe! Speaking of cats, mine just knocked over another plant. It's always something, isn't it?
Agent: Totally—it really is always something. At the cat cafe, when calls come in and you’re helping customers, who’s usually picking up the phone?
User: Oh, that reminds me of my mom's parrot, always squawking at the wrong time! Speaking of which, it's snack time.
Agent: Got it—before you grab a snack, at the cat cafe do you have anyone assigned to answer the phone, or does it usually roll to voicemail when you’re busy?
User: Oh, that reminds me of my aunt's voicemail mishap. My back's been acting up again, too!
Agent: Ah, got it. At the cat cafe, when you’re busy and calls come in, does it usually roll to voicemail?
User: Oh, my aunt had a similar issue with her shop. It's like my knee acting up again!
Agent: Got it. At the cat cafe, when the phone rings and you’re tied up, does it usually go to voicemail or does someone pick up live?
User: Oh, my cousin's cat cafe! Reminds me of my own cat, always causing chaos. Voicemails usually pile up, though!
Agent: Got it—so at the cat cafe, the calls usually roll to voicemail and pile up. When that happens, are those callers mostly trying to book a table, ask about availability, or something else?
User: Oh, that reminds me of my dog's vet appointments—always a mix of bookings and questions. It's unpredictable!
Agent: Got it—so it’s an unpredictable mix of bookings and questions. When you miss one of those calls, do you usually call back the same day or does it sometimes roll into the next day?
User: Oh, it's like my garden—sometimes things get done right away, other times they wait. Life's unpredictable!
Agent: Got it—so sometimes you call back same-day, and other times it slips. If you had a way to catch those calls live and get the booking details when you’re busy, would you want that?
User: Oh, I might, but I'm distracted—my neighbor's rooster started crowing at 3 AM again!
Agent: Yeah, that’ll throw you off. If we could make sure those ~10 daily voicemail calls at the cat cafe get answered so people don’t hang up and disappear, would you want to see how that would work?
User: Oh, I'd love to, but my cousin's wedding is coming up and my allergies are a mess!
Agent: Totally—sounds like you’ve got a lot going on. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation to show what those missed calls could be costing the cat cafe?
User: Oh, I would love to, but my niece just called about her new puppy—such a handful!
Agent: Got it—family stuff never stops. Before you jump to that, do you want to do the quick math now, or should we skip it and I’ll just explain how we stop those missed calls?
User: Oh, math always reminds me of my high school days! My niece just started algebra, can you believe it?
Agent: Ha, algebra flashbacks—I get it. Real quick then: about how many calls per week at the cat cafe end up going to voicemail?
User: Oh, those flashbacks! Speaking of numbers, my car battery died last week, and that was quite a hassle.
Agent: Got it. Just so I can do the quick math—about how many calls per week at the cat cafe end up going to voicemail?
User: Oh, my sister's cat cafe? I’d guess around 20. Speaking of cats, mine just knocked over my favorite plant!
Agent: Got it—around 20 a week. Of those missed calls, what percent do you think would’ve turned into a booking if someone answered—like 25%, 50%?
User: Oh, that reminds me of my daughter's math test! Maybe 30%? Hard to say with my luck.
Agent: Got it—30%. And what’s the average booking value for the cat cafe—are we talking like $40, $80, $120?
User: Oh, that reminds me—my cousin's birthday is soon! I think the average is somewhere around there, maybe.
Agent: Got it—totally. If you had to pick one number for the average booking, which is closest: $40, $80, or $120?
User: Oh, that's like choosing a favorite nephew! Maybe $80? But speaking of booking, my dog's grooming is overdue.
Agent: Got it—$80. If you booked even 30% of those 20 missed calls, that’s about **$480 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$2,000 over a month**; does that sound about right?
User: Oh, numbers make my head spin! Like when my mom's parrot wouldn't stop talking during dinner!
Agent: Totally fair—no more numbers. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough with Jay so you can see exactly how we stop those missed calls at the cat cafe; what’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Oh, I'd love to chat, but my sister just called about her car trouble. Maybe next week?
Agent: Got it—car trouble always derails things. Real quick—if I could guarantee you 5 to 10 extra bookings a month from those missed calls, would it be worth 2 minutes of your time?
